info.text: Formative quiz for Chapter 15. From Think Python, 3rd edition, by Allen B. Downey (https://allendowney.github.io/ThinkPython/), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

questiontext.text:
Suppose time is a Time object, and increment is an instance method defined in the Time class. What happens when we invoke increment like this?

time.increment(42)

answer.text: 42 is assigned to the first parameter of the method, and time is assigned to the second.

feedback.text: time is assigned to the first parameter of the method.

answer.text: This is an error because increment requires one argument and two are provided.

feedback.text: This method requires two arguments -- time is the first and 42 is the second.

answer.text: This is an error because increment requires two arguments and only one is provided.

feedback.text: Only one argument appears in parentheses, but time is passed to increment as the first argument.

answer.text: time is assigned to the first parameter of the method and 42 is assigned to the second.

feedback.text: time is assigned to the first parameter of the method, which is conventionally called self, and 42 is assigned to the second.

questiontext.text:
Suppose int_to_time is a static method defined in the Time class. What happens when we invoke int_to_time like this?

start = Time.int_to_time(34800)

answer.text: This is an error because int_to_time requires one argument and two are provided.

feedback.text: There is only one argument here, 34800.

answer.text: The Time class object is assigned to the first parameter of the method and 34800 is assigned to the second.

feedback.text: Because Time is a class, it is not passed as an argument.

answer.text: 34800 is assigned to the first parameter of the method and the Time class object is assigned to the second.

feedback.text: Because Time is a class, it is not passed as an argument.

answer.text: 34800 is assigned to the first parameter of int_to_time.

feedback.text: 34800 is assigned to the first parameter of int_to_time. Because Time is a class, it is not passed as an argument.

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?

answer.text: When we instantiate an object, its __init__ method is invoked.
When we use the + operator with an object, its __add__ method is invoked.
When we print an object, its __str__ method is invoked.
When we define a new class, its __init__ method is invoked.

feedback.text: Defining a new class does not invoke its __init__ method.
